description: This course covers the fundamentals of wireless networks, including radio frequency propagation, signal modulation techniques, and the IEEE 802.11 family of standards. Topics include wireless network architecture, mobility management, security protocols such as WPA3, and Quality of Service (QoS) mechanisms. The course also explores Bluetooth Low Energy (BLE), Zigbee, and LoRaWAN technologies, along with their applications in the Internet of Things (IoT). Students will study routing protocols like AODV and DSDV, and network optimization techniques such as channel allocation and interference management. The curriculum includes advanced topics such as 5G NR architecture, millimeter-wave communication, and cognitive radio systems. Specific algorithms and methods such as OFDMA, MIMO, and beamforming are examined in depth, with a focus on real-world deployment scenarios and industry standards.

clos.text: Define the key components of a wireless network, including radio frequency (RF) propagation, modulation techniques, and the IEEE 802.11 standards.
Describe the architecture and operation of wireless network protocols such as Bluetooth Low Energy (BLE), Zigbee, and LoRaWAN.
Explain the principles of mobility management, security protocols (e.g., WPA3), and Quality of Service (QoS) mechanisms in wireless networks.
Apply routing algorithms such as AODV and DSDV in the context of mobile ad hoc networks (MANETs) and evaluate their performance under varying network conditions.
Design and implement a wireless network solution using industry-standard tools, including simulation software for 5G NR and cognitive radio systems.

topics: Wireless Network Security: WPA3 and Beyond
